correctness.rationale: The stabilization-to-semigroup step is exact: after subtracting the \(j\) padding copies of \(1^k\), a fixed offset is eventually representable precisely when it lies in \(S_k\). Every even-base generator reduces recursively by \((2m)^k-1=(m^k-1)+m^k(2^k-1)\), leaving the odd generator \(A_k\) plus even odd-base generators. Splitting the coefficient of \(A_k\) by parity gives the disjoint decomposition. \(T_k\) is numerical because \(A_k\) is odd and \(\gcd(A_k,(A_k^k-1)/2)=1\). Even gaps of \(S_k\) are twice the positive gaps of \(T_k\); odd gaps consist of the \((A_k-1)/2\) positive odds below \(A_k\) plus \(A_k+2t\) for positive gaps \(t\) of \(T_k\). This yields the displayed Frobenius/genus formulas and parity. No finite table is used to infer the all-\(k\) theorem.
correctness.risk: The result proves the parity conjecture only; it does not settle the neighboring structural conjectures or give closed forms for \(F(T_k)\) or \(g(T_k)\).

final_claim: For every integer \(k\ge2\), if \(S_k=\langle n^k-1:n\ge2\rangle\), \(A_k=2^k-1\), and \(T_k=\langle A_k,(u^k-1)/2:u\ge3\text{ odd}\rangle\), then \(S_k=2T_k\sqcup(A_k+2T_k)\). Consequently the stabilized Waring-exception maximum and cardinality satisfy \(a_k=A_k+2F(T_k)\) and \(b_k=2g(T_k)+(A_k-1)/2\), so both are odd for all \(k\ge2\).
limitations: The finite source table and checker are corroborative only; the universal conclusion is supplied by the symbolic semigroup argument.
